title: 13 Villagers Carved This Cliff Tunnel by Hand, Not the State | China Travel Expert
description:
You'd assume a government crew blasted the Guoliang cliff tunnel through the Taihang Mountains. It was thirteen villagers, by hand.

Guoliang village sits on a cliff in the Taihang Mountains of Henan, and for centuries its only link to the outside world was a crumbling rock staircase called the "Sky Ladder." In 1972 a group of thirteen villagers, led by Shen Mingxin, began carving a road straight through the cliff — no power tools, just hammers and chisels. They sold livestock to buy roughly 4,000 hammers and 12 tons of steel, and at the hardest stretches progress was about one metre every three days. One villager died during the work. The 1.2 km tunnel — about 5 m high and 4 m wide, with "windows" punched through the rock face — opened on 1 May 1977 and turned the village into a destination.

🧭 Expert Tip: ride the little local bus slowly through the tunnel rather than driving — the 30-odd hand-cut window openings frame the valley, and you'll actually see the chisel marks.
